inline.s: The Doctrine of the Mean says: “What Heaven has imparted is called nature; to follow one’s nature is called the Way; to cultivate the Way is called teaching. The Way may not be departed from for even a single instant; what may be departed from is not the Way.” It also says: “Looking up to it, it grows ever higher; boring into it, it grows ever harder; gazing at it, it is before me; suddenly it is behind me.”
Mencius says: “It shines in the face, fills the back, and reaches to the four limbs, and the four limbs without a word convey it.”
The Heart Sutra says: “Avalokiteshvara Bodhisattva, while practicing deep prajnaparamita, clearly saw that the five aggregates are all empty and passed beyond all suffering and distress.”

The Jade Emperor’s Heart Sutra says: “The three fine medicines are spirit, qi, and essence.” It also says: “Issue from the mysterious and enter the female; as if lost, as if present; ceaselessly unbroken, firm the root and deep the stem.”
The sages of the three teachings all instruct later generations to comprehend this principle thoroughly, to rise above the sea of suffering, and together to enjoy heavenly bliss.

How pitiable that later people do not grasp its meaning, cannot enter the [school], and instead give rise to slander and abuse, deceiving the sages and destroying the worthies, affirming their own reasoning, giving themselves over to violence, and willfully sinking into the sea of suffering—such are criminals against Heaven and Earth.

I now urge the men and women of the world to turn back and reflect. The Buddhas of the three heavens all have the mind to save people and no intention to rebuke them. Therefore they teach people to refine their essence and transcend the world, to ascend together to the other shore.

How pitiable that men and women in their multitudes are sunk in confusion and never awaken. Their evil deeds pile up like a mountain, their offenses are deep as the sea. In good will we urge them, yet not only do they refuse to believe, they raise words of slander. It is like frost upon snow, cold water poured on ice—the more it accumulates the thicker it becomes; how can it ever melt away?
When offenses are piled up to the full, the last three inches of breath are cut off. When impermanence comes and wronged ghosts come to claim their due, can one escape?

There are some shameless men and women who, following their own nature, do not practice the right propriety, are used to devious ways, and dress alluringly, stirring up depraved minds. Men lure women with their looks, and women lure men; men and women enticing one another, they think themselves clever. Little do they know that in the yang world there are yang laws and in the yin realm there are yin statutes; the yang laws may be evaded, but the yin statutes are hard to escape.

I urge the resolute men and women of the world to turn back quickly, to mend their evil ways and follow the good, so that they may escape and avoid [the consequences], and thereby avoid the wrath of Heaven above.

Continuing from what was said above: the shameless men and women do not practice the right propriety, are set only on depraved lust, crave fine food, take the lives of creatures, and harm others to profit themselves. Such manifold unwholesomeness, heaping up boundless offenses—how can it be escaped?

I now point this out: men and women, turn back and think carefully. The body is the root of pain and distress; the eyes, ears, mouth, and nose are the gates that attract guilt. It was said before that nature and life transform into the hun and po [souls]; the hun and po dwell within, while the eyes, ears, nose, and tongue are without. The eyes, ears, nose, and tongue attract guilt and create offenses—why then should the nature-soul be convicted and punished for them?

When a person dies, the eyes, ears, nose, and tongue are all closed, and the single spirit-soul is led by impermanence before the King of Hell. Before the mirror of karma, good and evil stand clearly revealed, and every deed one has done is reflected one by one, and punishment is fixed according to the offense. The phantom body creates offenses, yet the reckoning is demanded of the nature-soul. Think it over carefully—what an injustice! It is like the saying: he eats the meat, and I repay the debt. Are we not harmed by it? Is the spirit not dragged down into avici?

Avici is hell. Offenses created in the living world are punished in the yin world. For oxen, horses, pigs, and sheep, the nature-soul must go to be reborn. Do the eyes, ears, nose, and tongue come to manage it for you? Think it over carefully—is it not a grief!

Our Buddha, compassionate, fearful that people cannot turn back and lose their human body, has specially spoken these words of direct pointing, like a blow and shout upon the head—truly the compassionate heart of our Buddha.

I too, understanding our Buddha, speak on behalf of the Dharma, pointing out and urging, so that men and women of the whole earth do not becloud their heaven-endowed nature but see through worldly affairs. Fame and profit are like floating clouds; wealth and honor are like a phantom dream. The love of husband and wife must one day come to parting. Though children fill the hall, when the great limit arrives they cannot take your place. Gold and silver, however much, cannot keep impermanence from arriving. One should examine oneself and awaken, and turn back in good time.

Seek out the perfected ones, who point to the supreme principle of nature and life, and receive the practice of refining the hun and mastering the po. Without, accumulate hidden merit to resolve the karmic enmities of many kalpas. Within, cultivate the wondrous fruit and realize nirvana, awaiting the lotus seat. When the three thousand merits are fulfilled and the eight hundred fruits are complete.

Heaven above will send down the elixir-book edict; like a cicada casting off its shell, one soars aloft to wait upon the supreme God. One’s rank is fixed by merit, and there is bestowed the immortal robe of five-zhong weight, the golden crown and jade hairpin, forever enjoying the heavenly peerage. The nine clans and seven ancestors alike enjoy heavenly bliss, never again to enter a womb, never again to descend into birth. Unborn and undying, free and at ease; among the three mountains and island paradises one wanders as one pleases—bliss without limit!
A gatha states:
Borrowing the false to cultivate the real—this subtlety is most rare; refining the hun and mastering the po—this is the true key;
Fearing that people wander heedless and never rest, I point straight and make of it a ladder to the sky.
